description:
## Problem
CI run 42453934266 (ubuntu x86_64, debug) on PR #280 aborts with 'thread <unknown> has overflowed its stack' while the lib test the_jit_runs_a_raising_loop_on_a_small_stack (src/exec/runtime_test.rs) compiles and runs fixture 00720 on a 256 KiB thread. The size was calibrated on arm64 and the in-process debug compiler and runtime need more than that on x86_64. The claim the test makes is right (A/B on the run door, macOS arm64 release: fixture 00720 under ulimit -s 512 exits 134 before fz-3ul.6 and 0 after; both pass at 1024), the instrument is wrong: a fixed thread size measures the ISA's baseline, not the property.

## Change
Measure the property directly, with telemetry (tests observe telemetry; add the event when it is missing).
- Process records the machine stack address at its quantum entry: Process::run_quantum (runtime/src/process.rs) stores the address of a local as the quantum's stack base before it enters compiled code, and the interpreter's quantum entry (where src/ir_interp runs a process's steps for one quantum) does the same; zero means no quantum is running.
- raise (runtime/src/failure.rs) computes the depth of the raise below that base (base minus the address of a local in raise, in bytes; 0 when the base is 0) and passes it to report_raise, which hands it to the raise observer beside kind, name and handler depth.
- RaiseRecord (src/exec/runtime.rs) gains stack_bytes: usize; the fz.runtime.raise telemetry event (src/telemetry/jsonl.rs) carries it; .agent/docs/runtime-telemetry.md documents the field, .agent/docs/exceptions.md states the invariant: every raise a loop delivers is at one of a handful of depths (the quantum entry path, the resumed-handler path, the resumed-yield path), never deeper with the iteration count.
- The test the_jit_runs_a_raising_loop_on_a_small_stack is replaced by one on the ordinary harness thread that runs 00720 through the JIT, collects the 100_000 RaiseRecords and asserts the set of distinct stack_bytes values has at most three members. No thread, no size. Interpreter twin asserts the same for the interpreter door.
- The derivation that makes the assertion loud: before fz-3ul.6 the handler ran in the raising call's place, so each iteration within a quantum added its frames and the depths formed a rising sequence of hundreds of distinct values; after it the handler resumes from the quantum entry so the depth repeats.

## Acceptance
- Red: the new assertion fails when the delivery is made to run in place again (builder shows it by a temporary local revert of the unwind, or by asserting on a synthetic record set; the former is preferred and must be undone) OR by running the test against telemetry replayed from the pre-.6 binary — pick the cheapest that proves the assertion discriminates, and say which.
- Green: the full gate: RUST_TEST_THREADS=1 cargo test --workspace --all-targets, cargo test --workspace --doc, cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings, cargo fmt --all -- --check.
- The 256 KiB-thread test is deleted (its claim lives in the new test).
- fixtures and goldens unchanged; the telemetry distiller and any golden that pins the fz.runtime.raise event shape updated if one exists (report which).
- CI on ubuntu x86_64 green after push (coordinator).
title: A raise reports its machine-stack depth, and the constant-stack test reads it
